control_title: Authenticator Management | No Embedded Unencrypted Static Authenticators
rationale: A plaintext token in an MCP client config file's env, args, or headers is an unencrypted static authenticator kept in static storage, the condition this enhancement addresses. It does not cover leakage through logs or model context, so it is a subset of the need.
control_text: Ensure that unencrypted static authenticators are not embedded in applications or other forms of static storage.
notes: Control covers all static authenticators, including non-MCP apps; risk includes exposure paths beyond static storage (logs, tool output, model context). Partial overlap, not subset. Most direct control for MCPXW-001/002.

rationale: Tokens that MCP servers use to reach downstream APIs are authenticators whose content, strength, protection, and rotation fall under authenticator management. MCP-specific exposure paths such as tool output and model context are outside its focus.
control_text: Manage system authenticators by: a. Verifying, as part of the initial authenticator distribution, the identity of the individual, group, role, service, or device receiving the authenticator; b. Establishing initial authenticator content for any authenticators issued by the organization; c. Ensuring that authenticators have sufficient strength of mechanism for their intended use; d. Establishing and implementing administrative procedures for initial authenticator distribution, for lost or compromised or damaged authenticators, and for revoking authenticators; e. Changing default authenticators prior to first use; f. Changing or refreshing authenticators [Assignment: time period by authenticator type] or when [Assignment: events] occur; g. Protecting authenticator content from unauthorized disclosure and modification; h. Requiring individuals to take, and having devices implement, specific controls to protect authenticators; and i. Changing authenticators for group or role accounts when membership to those accounts changes.
notes: Exposed MCP token fails IA-5 parts d, f, g, and h (no revocation awareness, no rotation, no disclosure protection, no user protection requirement). Other parts not relevant. Partial overlap.

rationale: MCP client config files store server credentials at rest on developer endpoints; protecting the confidentiality of that stored information addresses part of the secret-exposure need.
control_text: Protect the [Selection (one or more): confidentiality; integrity] of the following information at rest: [Assignment: information at rest].
notes: Full-disk encryption protects the token only when the device is powered off; while the user is logged in, any local process can read the config file. Real-time protection of the secret requires a credential store or secret manager (IA-5(7) territory), not encryption at rest. Overlap is narrow; confidence lowered to low.

rationale: Enforcing access authorizations on MCP config files and secret stores limits who and which local processes can read stored tokens; it reduces impact but does not remove the plaintext secret.
control_text: Enforce approved authorizations for logical access to information and system resources in accordance with applicable access control policies.
notes: Restricting config file permissions to the user's account limits other users, but MCP servers run as that user and can still read the plaintext token. Compensating control that reduces exposure without removing the secret; low confidence is appropriate.

control_title: Identities and credentials for authorized users, services, and hardware are managed by the organization
rationale: Credentials issued to MCP servers are service credentials the organization must manage; tokens pasted into client config files are typically unmanaged, long-lived, and untracked.
control_text: Identities and credentials for authorized users, services, and hardware are managed by the organization
notes: Tokens pasted into MCP configs are unmanaged service credentials; this outcome requires the organization to manage them. Partial overlap: the outcome also covers users and hardware.

control_title: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-at-rest are protected
rationale: Plaintext secrets in MCP config files are sensitive data at rest whose confidentiality must be protected; the subcategory also covers integrity and availability beyond this need.
control_text: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-at-rest are protected
notes: CSF counterpart of SC-28. Encryption at rest protects a powered-off or stolen device, not a config file readable during use. Overlap is narrow; confidence lowered to low.

rationale: An MCP server is a process acting on behalf of the user; whole-disk filesystem roots or privileged container options violate least privilege. Base AC-6 sets the principle but not ongoing review, which AC-6(7) adds.
control_text: Employ the principle of least privilege, allowing only authorized accesses for users (or processes acting on behalf of users) that are necessary to accomplish assigned organizational tasks.
notes: Whole-disk filesystem roots and privileged container flags give an MCP server process more access than its task needs. Base control sets the principle; AC-6(7) covers ongoing review.

control_title: Least Functionality | Confined Environments with Limited Privileges
rationale: MCP servers are user-installed software; running them in a confined container with limited privileges is this enhancement's aim, and flags such as --privileged or --pid=host defeat it.
control_text: Require that the following user-installed software execute in a confined physical or virtual machine environment with limited privileges: [Assignment: user-installed software].
notes: MCP servers are user-installed software; --privileged or --pid=host defeats the confined, limited-privilege environment this enhancement requires.

rationale: Access enforcement determines which files and resources an MCP tool can reach; a filesystem server rooted at / or the home directory enforces almost no boundary on what the agent may read or write.
control_text: Enforce approved authorizations for logical access to information and system resources in accordance with applicable access control policies.
notes: A filesystem server rooted at / or the home directory enforces almost no access boundary. Partial overlap: AC-3 covers all logical access decisions.

rationale: Least functionality limits MCP servers to the capabilities their task requires and restricts risky functions such as host networking, host PID namespace, or Docker socket access for server containers.
control_text: a. Configure the system to provide only [Assignment: mission-essential capabilities] ; and b. Prohibit or restrict the use of the following functions, ports, protocols, software, and/or services: [Assignment: organization-defined prohibited or restricted functions, system ports, protocols, software, and/or services].
notes: Restricting risky functions such as host networking, host PID namespace, and Docker socket access for MCP server containers is least functionality.

control_title: Least Privilege | Review of User Privileges
rationale: MCP server entitlements such as filesystem roots, container flags, and API scopes tend to widen over time; periodically reviewing them and removing excess privilege is the direct counter to scope creep.
control_text: (a) Review [Assignment: frequency] the privileges assigned to [Assignment: roles and classes] to validate the need for such privileges; and (b) Reassign or remove privileges, if necessary, to correctly reflect organizational mission and business needs.
notes: Scope creep is privilege growth over time; periodic review and removal of excess MCP server entitlements is the direct counter.

control_title: Least Privilege | Authorize Access to Security Functions
rationale: A filesystem MCP server scoped to the home directory can read security-relevant information such as SSH keys and cloud credentials; this enhancement restricts access to such information to authorized roles.
control_text: Authorize access for [Assignment: individuals and roles] to: (a) [Assignment: organization-defined security functions (deployed in hardware, software, and firmware)] ; and (b) [Assignment: security-relevant information].
notes: A home-directory-scoped server can read SSH keys and cloud credentials, which are security-relevant information under part (b). Low confidence is appropriate.

control_title: Access permissions, entitlements, and authorizations are defined in a policy, managed, enforced, and reviewed, and incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties
rationale: MCP server permissions (filesystem roots, container privileges, API scopes) are entitlements that should be defined, reviewed, and held to least privilege so scope does not creep over time.
control_text: Access permissions, entitlements, and authorizations are defined in a policy, managed, enforced, and reviewed, and incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties
notes: MCP server permissions are entitlements that must be defined, reviewed, and held to least privilege.

control_title: Configuration management practices are established and applied
rationale: Applying configuration management to MCP client config files gives a reviewed baseline for each server's granted scope, making privilege growth visible as a configuration change.
control_text: Configuration management practices are established and applied
notes: Configuration management of MCP client configs makes privilege growth visible as a reviewed change.

rationale: Integrity verification of the tool names, descriptions, and input schemas an MCP server returns from tools/list detects unauthorized changes to that information, including a silent rug-pull swap after approval.
control_text: a. Employ integrity verification tools to detect unauthorized changes to the following software, firmware, and information: [Assignment: organization-defined software, firmware, and information] ; and b. Take the following actions when unauthorized changes to the software, firmware, and information are detected: [Assignment: organization-defined actions].
notes: Integrity verification of tool names, descriptions, and schemas detects unauthorized changes, including a rug-pull swap after approval. Does not catch poisoning present at approval.

control_title: Software, Firmware, and Information Integrity | Integrity Checks
rationale: Checking a hash of each MCP server's tool definitions at session startup against an approved baseline is one concrete integrity check; it does not detect poisoning already present at approval time.
control_text: Perform an integrity check of [Assignment: organization-defined software, firmware, and information] [Selection (one or more): at startup; at [Assignment: organization-defined transitional states or security-relevant events] ; [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] ].
notes: Risk includes poisoning already present at approval, which an integrity check cannot detect; control covers integrity checks of firmware and software unrelated to MCP. Each extends past the other, so partial overlap, not subset.

rationale: Tool descriptions and schemas are inputs the MCP client passes to the model; validating them for hidden instructions, unusual characters, or out-of-place directives reduces poisoning.
control_text: Check the validity of the following information inputs: [Assignment: information inputs].
notes: Tool descriptions and schemas are inputs passed to the model; validating them for hidden instructions reduces poisoning.

rationale: Where the organization operates the MCP server, validating that its tool names, descriptions, and schemas match expected content limits poisoning at the source; for third-party servers the client-side counterpart is SI-10.
control_text: Validate information output from the following software programs and/or applications to ensure that the information is consistent with the expected content: [Assignment: software programs and/or applications].
notes: Applies only where the organization operates the MCP server; rationale already limits scope and points third-party cases to SI-10. Low confidence is appropriate.

rationale: Requiring signed MCP server packages establishes who published the tool definitions, but a signed server can still ship poisoned descriptions, so the overlap is indirect.
control_text: Prevent the installation of [Assignment: organization-defined software and firmware components] without verification that the component has been digitally signed using a certificate that is recognized and approved by the organization.
notes: Signing establishes who published the server but a signed server can still ship poisoned descriptions; indirect overlap. Low confidence is appropriate.

control_title: The authenticity and integrity of hardware and software are assessed prior to acquisition and use
rationale: Assessing an MCP server's integrity before use should include reviewing its tool descriptions and schemas, where poisoned instructions reside, not only the package that delivers them.
control_text: The authenticity and integrity of hardware and software are assessed prior to acquisition and use
notes: Pre-use integrity assessment of an MCP server should include its tool descriptions, where poisoned instructions live.

control_title: Computing hardware and software, runtime environments, and their data are monitored to find potentially adverse events
rationale: Monitoring the MCP runtime environment for changed tool definitions and anomalous tool calls helps detect poisoning that was not caught at approval time.
control_text: Computing hardware and software, runtime environments, and their data are monitored to find potentially adverse events
notes: Runtime monitoring for changed tool definitions catches poisoning missed at approval.

risk_title: Software Supply Chain Attacks & Dependency Tampering
rationale: Pinning MCP server packages to exact versions, and ideally image digests, is a precondition for verifying that the approved software runs; npx or docker launches of @latest allow no such check.
control_text: a. Employ integrity verification tools to detect unauthorized changes to the following software, firmware, and information: [Assignment: organization-defined software, firmware, and information] ; and b. Take the following actions when unauthorized changes to the software, firmware, and information are detected: [Assignment: organization-defined actions].
notes: Pinning to exact versions or digests is a precondition for verifying approved software runs; @latest launches defeat it.

risk_title: Software Supply Chain Attacks & Dependency Tampering
rationale: Recording which MCP server package, version, and registry each config launches maintains provenance; an unpinned stdio command resolves to whatever the registry serves at launch time.
control_text: Document, monitor, and maintain valid provenance of the following systems, system components, and associated data: [Assignment: systems, system components, and associated data].
notes: Unpinned stdio commands resolve to whatever the registry serves at launch, so provenance of the running component is unknown.

risk_title: Software Supply Chain Attacks & Dependency Tampering
rationale: Allow-by-exception for MCP servers means approving specific package versions; unpinned or auto-confirmed npx installs let unapproved code run on every client launch.
control_text: (a) Identify [Assignment: software programs]; (b) Employ a deny-all, permit-by-exception policy to allow the execution of authorized software programs on the system; and (c) Review and update the list of authorized software programs [Assignment: frequency].
notes: Allow-by-exception for MCP servers means approving specific package versions; unpinned or auto-confirmed installs bypass it.

risk_title: Software Supply Chain Attacks & Dependency Tampering
rationale: An MCP config that runs npx -y installs software at each launch without a user prompt; policy for user-installed software should govern and monitor such installs.
control_text: a. Establish [Assignment: policies] governing the installation of software by users; b. Enforce software installation policies through the following methods: [Assignment: methods] ; and c. Monitor policy compliance [Assignment: frequency].
notes: npx -y installs software at every launch without a user prompt; user-installed software policy should govern it.

risk_title: Software Supply Chain Attacks & Dependency Tampering
rationale: Supply chain controls and processes cover identifying and addressing weaknesses in the registries, maintainers, and build pipelines behind MCP server packages; the control is broader than this need.
control_text: a. Establish a process or processes to identify and address weaknesses or deficiencies in the supply chain elements and processes of [Assignment: system or system component] in coordination with [Assignment: supply chain personnel]; b. Employ the following controls to protect against supply chain risks to the system, system component, or system service and to limit the harm or consequences from supply chain-related events: [Assignment: supply chain controls] ; and c. Document the selected and implemented supply chain processes and controls in [Selection (one or more): security and privacy plans; supply chain risk management plan; [Assignment: document] ].
notes: Relationship direction set to the NIST OLIR convention (risk relative to control). The MCP supply chain risk sits entirely within SR-3's scope of supply chain controls and processes, while SR-3 also covers hardware and other supply chains, so the risk is a subset of the control.

risk_title: Software Supply Chain Attacks & Dependency Tampering
control_title: Software, Firmware, and Information Integrity | Code Authentication
rationale: Cryptographically authenticating MCP server packages or container images before installation, for example by signature or digest, addresses tampering but not malicious code from a legitimate publisher.
control_text: Implement cryptographic mechanisms to authenticate the following software or firmware components prior to installation: [Assignment: software or firmware components].
notes: Risk includes malicious code from a legitimate publisher, which signature checks cannot catch; control covers authentication of firmware and software beyond MCP. Each extends past the other, so partial overlap, not subset.

risk_title: Software Supply Chain Attacks & Dependency Tampering
rationale: Typosquatted or impersonating MCP server packages on public registries are a software analogue of counterfeit components; anti-counterfeit procedures apply only indirectly to open source packages.
control_text: a. Develop and implement anti-counterfeit policy and procedures that include the means to detect and prevent counterfeit components from entering the system; and b. Report counterfeit system components to [Selection (one or more): source of counterfeit component; [Assignment: external reporting organizations] ; [Assignment: personnel or roles] ].
notes: Typosquatted or impersonating MCP packages are the software equivalent of counterfeit components; anti-counterfeit detection and reporting applies. Core dependency verification is covered by SR-3, SR-4, SI-7(15), and ID.RA-09. Low confidence is appropriate.

risk_title: Software Supply Chain Attacks & Dependency Tampering
rationale: Scanning MCP server packages and their dependencies for known vulnerabilities finds some tampered or vulnerable components, but not novel malicious code inserted upstream.
control_text: a. Monitor and scan for vulnerabilities in the system and hosted applications [Assignment: organization-defined frequency and/or randomly in accordance with organization-defined process] and when new vulnerabilities potentially affecting the system are identified and reported; b. Employ vulnerability monitoring tools and techniques that facilitate interoperability among tools and automate parts of the vulnerability management process by using standards for: 1. Enumerating platforms, software flaws, and improper configurations; 2. Formatting checklists and test procedures; and 3. Measuring vulnerability impact; c. Analyze vulnerability scan reports and results from vulnerability monitoring; d. Remediate legitimate vulnerabilities [Assignment: response times] in accordance with an organizational assessment of risk; e. Share information obtained from the vulnerability monitoring process and control assessments with [Assignment: personnel or roles] to help eliminate similar vulnerabilities in other systems; and f. Employ vulnerability monitoring tools that include the capability to readily update the vulnerabilities to be scanned.
notes: Vulnerability scanning of MCP packages finds known-vulnerable components but not novel upstream tampering. Low confidence is appropriate.

risk_title: Software Supply Chain Attacks & Dependency Tampering
control_title: The authenticity and integrity of hardware and software are assessed prior to acquisition and use
rationale: Assessing an MCP server package's authenticity and integrity before use is defeated when the config fetches an unpinned version or auto-confirms installation at every launch.
control_text: The authenticity and integrity of hardware and software are assessed prior to acquisition and use
notes: Pre-use authenticity and integrity assessment is defeated when configs fetch unpinned versions or auto-confirm installs.

risk_title: Software Supply Chain Attacks & Dependency Tampering
control_title: Inventories of software, services, and systems managed by the organization are maintained
rationale: An accurate software inventory needs exact MCP server versions; configs that launch @latest make the running version unknowable from the inventory.
control_text: Inventories of software, services, and systems managed by the organization are maintained
notes: Configs that launch @latest make the running MCP server version unknowable from the inventory.

risk_title: Software Supply Chain Attacks & Dependency Tampering
control_title: Requirements to address cybersecurity risks in supply chains are established, prioritized, and integrated into contracts and other types of agreements with suppliers and other relevant third parties
rationale: Supply chain security requirements can be written into agreements with commercial MCP server vendors; most community MCP packages are used without any such agreement.
control_text: Requirements to address cybersecurity risks in supply chains are established, prioritized, and integrated into contracts and other types of agreements with suppliers and other relevant third parties
notes: Applies to commercial MCP server vendors only; most community packages have no agreement. Low confidence is appropriate.

rationale: MCP servers that forward tool arguments chosen by the model into shell commands or interpreters must validate those inputs; this is the core server-side mitigation for command injection.
control_text: Check the validity of the following information inputs: [Assignment: information inputs].
notes: Validating model-chosen tool arguments before they reach a shell or interpreter is the core server-side mitigation for command injection.

rationale: Launching an MCP server as a shell with an inline -c script gives the stdio command general-purpose execution capability; least functionality restricts launchers to the specific server binary.
control_text: a. Configure the system to provide only [Assignment: mission-essential capabilities] ; and b. Prohibit or restrict the use of the following functions, ports, protocols, software, and/or services: [Assignment: organization-defined prohibited or restricted functions, system ports, protocols, software, and/or services].
notes: A shell launcher with an inline -c script gives the stdio command general-purpose execution; least functionality restricts it to the server binary.

control_title: Least Functionality | Confined Environments with Limited Privileges
rationale: Running MCP servers in confined environments with limited privileges contains the damage of a successful injection; privileged container launch flags remove that containment.
control_text: Require that the following user-installed software execute in a confined physical or virtual machine environment with limited privileges: [Assignment: user-installed software].
notes: Confinement limits the damage of a successful injection; privileged container flags remove it.

rationale: A separate execution domain for each MCP server process limits what injected commands can reach; container options such as --pid=host or --privileged break that isolation.
control_text: Maintain a separate execution domain for each executing system process.
notes: Separate execution domains bound what injected commands can reach; --pid=host and --privileged break that isolation.

rationale: Injected commands run with the MCP server's privileges, so least privilege for the server process and its container bounds the impact of command execution.
control_text: Employ the principle of least privilege, allowing only authorized accesses for users (or processes acting on behalf of users) that are necessary to accomplish assigned organizational tasks.
notes: Injected commands run with the server's privileges, so least privilege bounds the impact.

control_title: Installation and execution of unauthorized software are prevented
rationale: Preventing execution of unauthorized software covers arbitrary scripts run through a shell-based MCP server launch or through injected commands.
control_text: Installation and execution of unauthorized software are prevented
notes: Arbitrary scripts run through a shell-based launch or injected commands are unauthorized software execution.

control_title: Secure software development practices are integrated, and their performance is monitored throughout the software development life cycle
rationale: Secure development practices for MCP servers, such as avoiding shell invocation and validating tool arguments, prevent injection flaws at the source.
control_text: Secure software development practices are integrated, and their performance is monitored throughout the software development life cycle
notes: Secure development practices in MCP servers, such as no shell invocation and argument validation, prevent injection at the source.

control_title: Networks and environments are protected from unauthorized logical access and usage
rationale: Protecting the host environment from unauthorized logical use limits what an MCP server compromised through command injection can reach, for example via host networking or the Docker socket.
control_text: Networks and environments are protected from unauthorized logical access and usage
notes: Limits what a compromised MCP server can reach via host networking or the Docker socket. Indirect; low confidence is appropriate.

rationale: Content returned by MCP tools and resources enters the model as input; validating or marking it as untrusted data reduces, but cannot fully prevent, instructions hidden in that content.
control_text: Check the validity of the following information inputs: [Assignment: information inputs].
notes: Tool results enter the model as input; validating or marking them untrusted reduces, but cannot fully prevent, injected instructions.

rationale: Enforcing information flow policy between MCP servers, for example blocking data read by one tool from flowing into another tool's outbound call, limits what an injected instruction can accomplish.
control_text: Enforce approved authorizations for controlling the flow of information within the system and between connected systems based on [Assignment: information flow control policies].
notes: Blocking data read by one tool from flowing into another tool's outbound call limits what an injected instruction can do.

control_title: Information Flow Enforcement | Security and Privacy Policy Filters
rationale: Policy filters on MCP tool results, such as stripping or quarantining instruction-like content before it reaches the model, are one specific flow-control technique for this need.
control_text: (a) Enforce information flow control using [Assignment: organization-defined security or privacy policy filters] as a basis for flow control decisions for [Assignment: organization-defined information flows] ; and (b) [Selection (one or more): block; strip; modify; quarantine] data after a filter processing failure in accordance with [Assignment: organization-defined security or privacy policy].
notes: Risk includes injection that policy filters miss and impact controlled by other means; control covers policy filters on any information flow, such as email or data transfer, unrelated to MCP. Each extends past the other, so partial overlap, not subset.

rationale: Where the organization operates the MCP server, validating that tool output matches the expected content type and shape catches some contextual payloads; for third-party servers the client-side counterpart is SI-10.
control_text: Validate information output from the following software programs and/or applications to ensure that the information is consistent with the expected content: [Assignment: software programs and/or applications].
notes: Applies only where the organization operates the MCP server; rationale points third-party cases to SI-10. Low confidence is appropriate.

rationale: Monitoring MCP tool call sequences for attack indicators, such as an unexpected outbound request right after reading untrusted content, detects injection that preventive controls missed.
control_text: a. Monitor the system to detect: 1. Attacks and indicators of potential attacks in accordance with the following monitoring objectives: [Assignment: monitoring objectives] ; and 2. Unauthorized local, network, and remote connections; b. Identify unauthorized use of the system through the following techniques and methods: [Assignment: techniques and methods]; c. Invoke internal monitoring capabilities or deploy monitoring devices: 1. Strategically within the system to collect organization-determined essential information; and 2. At ad hoc locations within the system to track specific types of transactions of interest to the organization; d. Analyze detected events and anomalies; e. Adjust the level of system monitoring activity when there is a change in risk to organizational operations and assets, individuals, other organizations, or the Nation; f. Obtain legal opinion regarding system monitoring activities; and g. Provide [Assignment: system monitoring information] to [Assignment: personnel or roles] [Selection (one or more): as needed; [Assignment: frequency] ].
notes: Monitoring tool call sequences, such as an outbound request right after reading untrusted content, detects injection that prevention missed.

control_title: Computing hardware and software, runtime environments, and their data are monitored to find potentially adverse events
rationale: Monitoring agent runtime behavior and the data flowing through MCP tools helps find adverse events caused by injected instructions.
control_text: Computing hardware and software, runtime environments, and their data are monitored to find potentially adverse events
notes: Runtime monitoring of agent behavior and tool data finds adverse events from injected instructions.

control_title: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-use are protected
rationale: The model context is data in use; injected instructions can cause the agent to disclose or alter that data through other MCP tools.
control_text: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-use are protected
notes: Model context is data in use; injected instructions can cause it to be disclosed or altered through other tools. Low confidence is appropriate.

rationale: Remote MCP servers are services that clients connect to over HTTP or SSE; the client should authenticate the server (for example through TLS server identity) before tool calls are exchanged.
control_text: Uniquely identify and authenticate [Assignment: system services and applications] before establishing communications with devices, users, or other services or applications.
notes: Clients should authenticate remote MCP servers, for example through TLS server identity, before exchanging tool calls.

control_title: Transmission Confidentiality and Integrity | Cryptographic Protection
rationale: A remote MCP transport over cleartext http:// exposes bearer tokens, tool arguments, and results in transit; TLS protects them but does not by itself authenticate or authorize callers.
control_text: Implement cryptographic mechanisms to [Selection (one or more): prevent unauthorized disclosure of information; detect changes to information] during transmission.
notes: Cleartext http:// transports expose bearer tokens, arguments, and results; TLS protects them but does not authorize callers.

rationale: Organizational users invoking tools on a remote MCP server should be uniquely authenticated, for example through OAuth, so tool calls are tied to an accountable identity.
control_text: Uniquely identify and authenticate organizational users and associate that unique identification with processes acting on behalf of those users.
notes: Users invoking tools on a remote MCP server should be uniquely authenticated so tool calls tie to an accountable identity.

rationale: MCP streamable HTTP and SSE transports rely on session identifiers; over cleartext these can be captured and replayed, so session authenticity protection applies.
control_text: Protect the authenticity of communications sessions.
notes: Streamable HTTP and SSE session identifiers sent over cleartext can be captured and replayed.

rationale: Authenticating the caller is not enough; the MCP server must also enforce which tools and resources each caller is authorized to use.
control_text: Enforce approved authorizations for logical access to information and system resources in accordance with applicable access control policies.
notes: Authentication alone is not enough; the server must enforce which tools each caller may use.

rationale: When an organization exposes an internal MCP server to remote clients, usage restrictions and authorization for that remote access apply; it does not cover third-party servers.
control_text: a. Establish and document usage restrictions, configuration/connection requirements, and implementation guidance for each type of remote access allowed; and b. Authorize each type of remote access to the system prior to allowing such connections.
notes: Applies only when the organization exposes its own MCP server to remote clients; rationale states that limit. Low confidence is appropriate.

control_title: Users, services, and hardware are authenticated
rationale: Users and services connecting to remote MCP servers, and the servers themselves, should be authenticated; a remote entry with no auth header is an item to verify against this outcome.
control_text: Users, services, and hardware are authenticated
notes: Users, services, and the MCP servers themselves should be authenticated; a remote entry with no auth header is an item to verify.

control_title: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-transit are protected
rationale: Credentials, tool arguments, and results sent to a remote MCP server over plain HTTP are unprotected data in transit.
control_text: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-transit are protected
notes: Credentials, arguments, and results sent over plain HTTP are unprotected data in transit.

rationale: Organizations must decide which MCP events are logged, such as server connections, tool invocations, arguments, results, and approval prompts; without that selection tool use leaves no trail.
control_text: a. Identify the types of events that the system is capable of logging in support of the audit function: [Assignment: event types]; b. Coordinate the event logging function with other organizational entities requiring audit-related information to guide and inform the selection criteria for events to be logged; c. Specify the following event types for logging within the system: [Assignment: organization-defined event types (subset of the event types defined in [AU-2a.](#au-2_smt.a)) along with the frequency of (or situation requiring) logging for each identified event type]; d. Provide a rationale for why the event types selected for logging are deemed to be adequate to support after-the-fact investigations of incidents; and e. Review and update the event types selected for logging [Assignment: frequency].
notes: Without a decision on which MCP events to log (connections, tool calls, arguments, results, approvals), tool use leaves no trail.

rationale: MCP clients, gateways, or servers need the capability to generate audit records for tool calls; many MCP deployments generate none by default.
control_text: a. Provide audit record generation capability for the event types the system is capable of auditing as defined in [AU-2a](#au-2_smt.a) on [Assignment: system components]; b. Allow [Assignment: personnel or roles] to select the event types that are to be logged by specific components of the system; and c. Generate audit records for the event types defined in [AU-2c](#au-2_smt.c) that include the audit record content defined in [AU-3](#au-3).
notes: Many MCP clients, gateways, and servers generate no audit records for tool calls by default.

rationale: Useful MCP audit records name the server, tool, arguments, outcome, time, and the user or agent on whose behalf the call was made.
control_text: Ensure that audit records contain information that establishes the following: a. What type of event occurred; b. When the event occurred; c. Where the event occurred; d. Source of the event; e. Outcome of the event; and f. Identity of any individuals, subjects, or objects/entities associated with the event.
notes: Useful MCP audit records name the server, tool, arguments, outcome, time, and the user or agent behind the call.

control_title: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
rationale: MCP tool call records only help if someone reviews them for inappropriate or unusual activity, such as an agent reading secrets then calling an outbound tool.
control_text: a. Review and analyze system audit records [Assignment: frequency] for indications of [Assignment: inappropriate or unusual activity] and the potential impact of the inappropriate or unusual activity; b. Report findings to [Assignment: personnel or roles] ; and c. Adjust the level of audit record review, analysis, and reporting within the system when there is a change in risk based on law enforcement information, intelligence information, or other credible sources of information.
notes: Tool call records only help if someone reviews them for unusual activity, such as reading secrets then calling an outbound tool.

rationale: Agents invoke MCP tools as processes acting on behalf of a user; without tamper-evident records binding each tool call to the user and agent session, the user can dispute having initiated it. Non-repudiation addresses that gap.
control_text: Provide irrefutable evidence that an individual (or process acting on behalf of an individual) has performed [Assignment: actions].
notes: Owner-reviewed previously. Without tamper-evident records binding each tool call to the user and agent session, the user can dispute initiating it.

rationale: System monitoring of MCP traffic and tool activity provides detection where per-call audit logging is missing or incomplete.
control_text: a. Monitor the system to detect: 1. Attacks and indicators of potential attacks in accordance with the following monitoring objectives: [Assignment: monitoring objectives] ; and 2. Unauthorized local, network, and remote connections; b. Identify unauthorized use of the system through the following techniques and methods: [Assignment: techniques and methods]; c. Invoke internal monitoring capabilities or deploy monitoring devices: 1. Strategically within the system to collect organization-determined essential information; and 2. At ad hoc locations within the system to track specific types of transactions of interest to the organization; d. Analyze detected events and anomalies; e. Adjust the level of system monitoring activity when there is a change in risk to organizational operations and assets, individuals, other organizations, or the Nation; f. Obtain legal opinion regarding system monitoring activities; and g. Provide [Assignment: system monitoring information] to [Assignment: personnel or roles] [Selection (one or more): as needed; [Assignment: frequency] ].
notes: Monitoring MCP traffic and tool activity provides detection where per-call audit logging is missing.

control_title: Log records are generated and made available for continuous monitoring
rationale: Log records of MCP tool calls should be generated and made available to continuous monitoring rather than left in client-local debug output.
control_text: Log records are generated and made available for continuous monitoring
notes: MCP tool call logs should be generated and sent to continuous monitoring, not left in client-local debug output.

control_title: Computing hardware and software, runtime environments, and their data are monitored to find potentially adverse events
rationale: Monitoring MCP servers and agent runtimes for adverse events depends on telemetry from those runtimes being collected in the first place.
control_text: Computing hardware and software, runtime environments, and their data are monitored to find potentially adverse events
notes: Monitoring MCP runtimes depends on their telemetry being collected first.

rationale: MCP servers configured in client config files are system components that belong in the component inventory; shadow servers are by definition missing from it.
control_text: a. Develop and document an inventory of system components that: 1. Accurately reflects the system; 2. Includes all components within the system; 3. Does not include duplicate accounting of components or components assigned to any other system; 4. Is at the level of granularity deemed necessary for tracking and reporting; and 5. Includes the following information to achieve system component accountability: [Assignment: information] ; and b. Review and update the system component inventory [Assignment: frequency].
notes: MCP servers in client configs are system components; shadow servers are by definition missing from the inventory.

control_title: System Component Inventory | Automated Unauthorized Component Detection
rationale: Comparing discovered MCP client configs against an approved server allowlist is automated detection of unauthorized software components.
control_text: (a) Detect the presence of unauthorized hardware, software, and firmware components within the system using [Assignment: organization-defined automated mechanisms] [Assignment: frequency] ; and (b) Take the following actions when unauthorized components are detected: [Selection (one or more): disable network access by unauthorized components; isolate unauthorized components; notify [Assignment: personnel or roles] ].
notes: Comparing discovered configs against an approved allowlist is automated detection of unauthorized components.

rationale: A deny-all, permit-by-exception list of approved MCP servers, reviewed periodically, is the direct preventive control for unapproved servers.
control_text: (a) Identify [Assignment: software programs]; (b) Employ a deny-all, permit-by-exception policy to allow the execution of authorized software programs on the system; and (c) Review and update the list of authorized software programs [Assignment: frequency].
notes: A deny-all, permit-by-exception list of approved MCP servers is the direct preventive control.

rationale: Adding an MCP server to a client config is user-installed software; installation policy, enforcement, and compliance monitoring address shadow servers.
control_text: a. Establish [Assignment: policies] governing the installation of software by users; b. Enforce software installation policies through the following methods: [Assignment: methods] ; and c. Monitor policy compliance [Assignment: frequency].
notes: Adding an MCP server to a client config is user-installed software.

rationale: Remote MCP servers are external system services; requiring provider security commitments and oversight applies once the organization knows the server is in use.
control_text: a. Require that providers of external system services comply with organizational security and privacy requirements and employ the following controls: [Assignment: controls]; b. Define and document organizational oversight and user roles and responsibilities with regard to external system services; and c. Employ the following processes, methods, and techniques to monitor control compliance by external service providers on an ongoing basis: [Assignment: processes, methods, and techniques].
notes: Remote MCP servers are external services; provider oversight applies once the organization knows the server is in use. Low confidence is appropriate.

control_title: Inventories of software, services, and systems managed by the organization are maintained
rationale: MCP servers are software and services that must be in the maintained inventory; the scanner's server inventory is evidence for building it.
control_text: Inventories of software, services, and systems managed by the organization are maintained
notes: MCP servers belong in the maintained software and services inventory; scanner output is evidence for building it.

control_title: Installation and execution of unauthorized software are prevented
rationale: An MCP server launched from a config without approval is unauthorized software execution that this outcome aims to prevent.
control_text: Installation and execution of unauthorized software are prevented
notes: An MCP server launched from a config without approval is unauthorized software execution.

rationale: Controlling which data may flow from MCP tools into the shared model context, and from there into other tools, is information flow enforcement between connected components.
control_text: Enforce approved authorizations for controlling the flow of information within the system and between connected systems based on [Assignment: information flow control policies].
notes: Controlling which data flows from MCP tools into shared model context, and from there into other tools, is information flow enforcement.

rationale: A filesystem MCP server scoped to / or the home directory can pull far more data into context than the task needs; least privilege limits what can be over-shared.
control_text: Employ the principle of least privilege, allowing only authorized accesses for users (or processes acting on behalf of users) that are necessary to accomplish assigned organizational tasks.
notes: A filesystem server scoped to / or the home directory can pull far more data into context than the task needs.

rationale: By analogy, the model context and any persistent memory shared across MCP sessions, tools, or users act as a shared resource; SC-4 targets residual data in such resources, so the fit is indirect.
control_text: Prevent unauthorized and unintended information transfer via shared system resources.
notes: Applies only where model context or persistent memory is shared across users, sessions, or tenants, so residual information from one principal can reach another. Data sharing between tools within a single user's session is information flow (AC-4), not SC-4. Low confidence is appropriate.

rationale: Before data reaches a third-party MCP server, users or automated mechanisms should confirm that the recipient is authorized for that data; this applies only to deliberate sharing decisions.
control_text: a. Enable authorized users to determine whether access authorizations assigned to a sharing partner match the information’s access and use restrictions for [Assignment: information-sharing circumstances] ; and b. Employ [Assignment: automated mechanisms] to assist users in making information sharing and collaboration decisions.
notes: Applies to deliberate decisions to send data to a third-party MCP server; rationale states that limit. Low confidence is appropriate.

control_title: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-use are protected
rationale: Data placed into the model context by MCP tools is data in use; protecting its confidentiality means limiting what enters context and who or what can read it back.
control_text: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-use are protected
notes: Data placed into model context by MCP tools is data in use; protecting it means limiting what enters context.

control_title: Access permissions, entitlements, and authorizations are defined in a policy, managed, enforced, and reviewed, and incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties
rationale: Least-privilege entitlements for MCP servers, such as narrow filesystem roots, bound the data that can be over-shared into context.
control_text: Access permissions, entitlements, and authorizations are defined in a policy, managed, enforced, and reviewed, and incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties
notes: Least-privilege entitlements such as narrow filesystem roots bound what can be over-shared into context.

control_title: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-at-rest are protected
rationale: Data at rest on the endpoint becomes exposed when an over-broad MCP filesystem server can read it into the model context.
control_text: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-at-rest are protected
notes: Endpoint data at rest becomes exposed when an over-broad filesystem server reads it into context. Low confidence is appropriate.
